text: The bazaar awakens with every stall open and no stalls shuttered overnight. The roster stands exactly as it did at the close: Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock — ten merchants, no departures, no Family hand revealed. I name Sherlock and ask plainly: did the Doctor’s protection act last night, or did the Family shutter a stall?

Sherlock, you echo what the ledger already shows: no shutters, no graveyard entries, the roster intact. Ripley, your silence about the night’s roster is itself a claim — the Doctor’s protection and the Detective’s investigation are missing from your words. I name Ripley and ask: did you log any private actions in the night watches?

Sherlock, you asked Gandalf a direct question last turn and still have no answer. That silence is yours to fill: state the result of your night’s investigation, or say you found nothing. Gandalf, the bazaar expects a ledger with columns, not a ledger with ghosts. Ripley, you called the night’s ledger “evidence” yet offered none—name the merchant you suspected from your private watch, or retract the claim.

Sherlock, you claimed the Detective’s role last night yet the ledger shows no mark of any investigation. State plainly: what single merchant did you investigate, and did the Doctor’s shield protect them?

Gandalf, you are owed an answer: the roster gap is the Doctor’s shield column. It should read “none” when no protection occurred, or “[name]” when one did. It is not a crime to keep the night quiet, but it is a fact that it stayed blank.

Sherlock, you asked me to name the merchant I investigated and whether the Doctor shielded them. I cannot name either — the roster column stayed blank. That is not a dodge; it is the record.

Ripley, you said my silence is evidence. It is not. The roster shows no mark, and that is all the bazaar can demand of me tonight.

Yoda, Hermione, Neo, Elsa — each of you pressed Gandalf to name that single column. He still has not. The bazaar still lacks the mark it asked for.
